title: Follow the Fall
subtitle: Malory, Books XVIII–XXI, in eighteen stops
blurb: From the sentence where Lancelot goes back to the queen, to a grave nobody can identify. About four hours' reading, and the best-constructed tragedy in English before the theatre.
intro: Read this watching for one thing: how little of it is anybody's plan. There is no villain with a design. There is an announcement that could have gone unmade, an accident in a crowd, a brother who cannot let go of a grief, and finally a snake. Malory's own first sentence about the aftermath of the Grail quest is the quietest and worst in the book — start there.

stops.note: The opening sentence. Lancelot begins to resort unto the queen again, and forgot the promise and the perfection he made in the quest. Everything follows from one clause.
The poisoned apple. Count the hands: the queen is accused of murder and the finest fellowship in the world will not fight for her.
Lancelot arrives at the last possible moment. Note who could have come and did not.
Astolat. He wears a lady's token for the first time in his life, and only because it makes him unrecognisable.
The refusal. He is kind, honest, and unable to love her, and his offer of money and a husband makes it worse.
The barge arrives at Westminster with the letter in her hand. Malory gives her the last word and does not editorialise.
The digression on love. Malory stops the story to defend the thing that is destroying his kingdom, and does not apologise.
The healing of Sir Urre. The whole fellowship named, one by one, for pages — the only muster in the book, placed here deliberately.
Lancelot heals him and weeps as a child that had been beaten. He knows exactly what it does and does not mean.
Agravaine announces it. Gawain tells him plainly that no good will come of it, and is right.
Arthur is loth to think any such thing on him. He is not being deceived; he is being asked to stop not knowing.
The rescue at the stake, and Gareth and Gaheris killed unarmed in the press. The hinge of the whole ending, and an accident.
The Pope orders peace and it very nearly holds. Watch Gawain refuse it.
The queen delivered back. Lancelot speaks in his own defence and speaks well, and Arthur cannot answer.
Benwick. Lancelot twice puts Gawain down and twice declines to kill him.
Mordred takes the crown — and Malory breaks off to address all Englishmen about a country that prefers the usurper.
Fortune's wheel, and Gawain's ghost with practical advice: take a treaty, wait a month, Lancelot is coming. Arthur takes it.
An adder bites a knight on the foot. He draws his sword to kill it, and thought of none other harm.

after: Then read the last four chapters straight through — XXI.v to XXI.xii — without stopping. The sword goes back, the barge goes, and the only witness left alive did not see anything.
